state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on the misconception of ignoring the negative sign when expanding brackets. Remember, when multiplying two negatives, the result is positive. Let's revisit the steps to correctly expand the brackets in your expression \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) and identify the terms that contain \( x^{2} \). Can you explain why the terms should be \( +6x^{2} \), \( -3x^{2} \), and \( +5x^{2} \)?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I see what you mean about the negative sign. So when I expand \( (x-3)(x+6) \), I should get \( -3x \) from the \( -3 \) times \( x \) and \( -18 \) from the \( -3 \) times \( 6 \). But I’m still confused about how to combine those with the other terms. Can you help me figure out how to find all the \( x^{2} \) terms correctly?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on correctly expanding the remaining brackets \( (x+5) \) and \( (x+6) \). Remember to multiply each term in one bracket by every term in the other bracket. This will help you identify all the \( x^{2} \) terms in the expression. Can you try expanding these brackets and see if you can correctly identify the terms that contain \( x^{2} \)?
